(iii) for issuance of any appropriate writ or writs, rule or direction as your lordships may deem fit and proper to the facts and circumstances of the case as well as for which the petitioner may be found entitled thereto.
3. A counter affidavit of the respondent nos. 5 to 7 and 9 is on record and the learned counsel has taken this Court to para-14 to show that the writ petitioner received compensation and six years later, the present writ petition has Patna High Court CWJC No.15812 of 2017(2) dt.05-05-2025 been filed.
4. This counter affidavit was served to the learned counsel for the petitioner in the year 2018 and there is no reply to it.
5. Be that as it may, since there is no appearance, the writ petition is dismissed for non-prosecution.
